text: After playing Tomb Raider: Anniversary, this part of the Tomb Raider Saga fails to succeed it's sequel, although it is clearly a large improvement over the infamous Tomb Raider: Angel of Darkness. Even though the game features different locations all over the world it also lacks the actual feeling of being an actual 'tomb raider'; the levels are very often urban oder industrial structures, for example a devastated soviet laboratory in the ice desert of Kazahkstan or a yakuza penthouse in Tokio. Furthermore the leveldesign is not as challenging as it is in other titles of the series. The puzzles are too easy and the focus on combat is too big. The playtime for a walkthroug with about 5 hours for a skilled player is devinately pretty low. It's not a bad game, you can really see how the developers tried to bring a new refreshed version of a Tomb Raider game and in this point they did a good job, it's still a fun game. But for me, there is plenty of possibilitys to improve. I would still recommend it because if you can overlook the fact, that this game does not try to bring you the original Tomb Raider feeling but instead it tries to bring you a new expierience, you will have a good time. Even though it's not great.

title: tomb raider: legend
text: Tomb Raider Legend has an interesting storyline (although I don't really think it matters any more since the series has been rebooted again). The game offers a wide range of environments to explore, with each level taking place at a different country, and the game-play seems to vary depending on the level, as some level focus more on attacking enemies, while other level focus on traditional tomb raiding and action adventure. Since this entry was supposed to be the reboot of the Tomb Raider franchise, a lot of changes were made. Some are good and some are not very good. Legend is just very different from Core Design's classic Tomb Raider games overall. However, I have to warn you that this game is very, very SHORT. [Light Spoiler] It contains only 7 major levels and the Croft Manor. In fact,  I think it is the same length as Tomb Raider Chronicles or maybe even shorter. Furthermore, TR Legend only presents the first halves of the Tomb Raider Trilogy story as the second halves of the story is told in Underworld.  To make up for this, this game does contain a lot of bonus contents and secrets. My advice is that if you are new to the series because of Tomb Raider (2013), and you are interested in a game with interesting story , you should play it. If not, you should probably wait for it to be on sale again.

title: tomb raider: legend
text: A bit of modern action, a bit of classic platforming and a hearty serving of badarse Lara makes for a nice, hearty dish! Crystal Dynamics managed to strike a great balance of moden tendencies of gaming (even the ones I don't appreciate, like QTEs, but thankfully, they don't happen very often) and the platforming, acrobatic, risk-of-falling-to-your-death-at-every-moment wholesome goodness. And what I really, really enjoyed? Actual TOMB RAIDING! I really enjoyed and liked all the levels, but King Arthur's tomb ... man, that level was the bee's knees - I loved every minute of it! So what holds this game from being perfect? Well, apart from the QTEs I already mentioned, I'd point out wobbly, awkward controls which I didn't really like. They're far from being useless and frustrating, but not nearly perfect either. Also, the characters and the story didn't really grab me at all; the story especially seemed a bit half-baked to me, which is a shame - I always loved the stories in Tomb Raider games. Another negative thing would be very easy puzzles and boss fights. The game is generally pretty easy, but the puzzles and boss fights were just way too easy. I played the game on the normal difficulty, so maybe I'll try it on hard, but seriously, normal difficulty is really way too easy. As far as characters go, they were very, very unremarkable, including both the goodies and the baddies. Oh well, at least Lara was portrayed well. I really enjoyed her voice actress, too - she has a very nice, agreeable voice that really suits Lara very well. I also loved how angry Lara got at the end of the game, you don't see that very often. All in all, even in spite of these flaws, this is a fine reboot of a legendary franchise, and a solid, solid game. A few shortcomings, but a whole lot of goodness. I appreciate Crystal Dynamics' success in fusing modern game sensibilities with the classic Tomb Raider attributes we old school TR fans know and love. Legend is definitely a worthy volume in this legendary franchise, and a fine example of how reboots should be made.

text: I prefer more action-oriented games (i.e. Uncharted series). But this was an enjoyable change of pace because as expected, it's more about solving puzzles then shootouts like the Uncharted series. This game has nice graphics and design of environment, good sound, satisfactory cutscenes to make the story go along and make it not just seem like a game one puzzle solving level after another that I got from Tomb Raider Anniversary especially. Lara's movements are cool (e.g. melee kicking, able to jump off walls in tight spaces back and forth so it looks martial-arts like, can equip weapons instead of having to find them). There's a satisfactory amount of gun shooting in a game that is mostly puzzle solving and exploring. Norse mythology is used nicely as a plot point. And a big plus: the camera angles sometimes leads to Lara's nice♥♥♥♥♥ and you can choose her outfit and beginning of levels (her swimsuit in particular is eye-catching :p). Major gripes I have with this game: controls not 100% smooth (e.g. jumping to a moving object and she appears to have reached it but suddenly she drops to her death, and couple of times I was stuck in a random spot) And the camera auto adjusts so it gets really annoying trying to see your surrounding while moving. If this game was in the 100% yes or 100% no pile of games to play again, I would put this in the yes pile. I definitely found it more enjoyable than Tomb Raider Anniversary and Tomb Raider Legend. This game for me is a 8.5/10, a solid adventure game.

text: Tomb Raider Underworld aka Pot Smasher 2008 edition Pros - beautiful landscapes and vistas - the graphics are really good (REALLY GOOD) - clever puzzles that make you think, without throwing the controller through the window in rage - amazing level design - quite a lot of attention to small details, which add a lot of credibility to the game and setting as a whole - Lara´s movement feels more realistic - the checkpoint system is no longer frustrating thus far this could easily be a 10/10 game, but then again, you have to remember the Cons - probably the worst camera I´ve ever encountered in a game - as in, REALLY, REALLY AWFUL CAMERA - a lot of annoying deaths, due to said camera, which make you throw the controller through the window in rage - there are some bugs here and there, and I had some weird framerate drops a few times - also, the story is kind of meh - did I mention the camera is terrible? misc - you´ll be breaking/smashing  A LOT of pots and vases throughout the game, one would have thought Lara cared for archeological stuff, but apparently not - there are lizard and spider enemies that climb on walls, so you can no longer hang down from a ledge and shoot the enemies from a safe distance Conclusion If you liked previous titles, this game is BETTER. However, do expect to rage over unfair deaths caused by the bad camera. I would probably rate it 8/10 though, as the positive really outweighs the negative in the long run. I would actually go so far as to say that this is THE BEST Tomb Raider game in my opinion (Tomb Raider 2013 does not count since there is no actual tomb raiding involved, and Underworld would even outshine this if not for the camera). 8/10 would definitely smash huge amounts of randomly placed pots again

title: tomb raider: underworld
text: I loved this game. I have the other two in the trilogy - Anniversary and Legend. However, this one is for the PC, my others for PS2. To compare them: Story is best in Underworld, but also great in Legend. Anniversary I found did not have enough story, with a basic plotline, but I get it was a remake of a classic. There's always something happeneign in Underworld, cutscenes in every level. So many surprises in Underworld, and I like that it takes a darker turn. Rewards are not as good. There are a larger amount of treasures to find than in Legend, but I can't remember in comparison to Anniversary (are there more in Anniversary?). The rewards are all concept art and character designs. No unlockable outfits, bringing me to ... Outfits. Smallest selection available in the trilogy. You cannot 'unlock' any, but the selection is available from the start. At each level you are given a choice of 2 - 3 outfits corresponding with the location (you can't play with winter clothes in Thailand). Graphics are amazing. I love the difference. I'm not usually one interested in graphics, but this changed me. I don't know if it's just PC vs PS2, but they helped so much for me. Seeing Amanda again with better graphics really changed the game for me. Although, seeing Lara in some scenes she looks so much older! Moves have definately been improved. Lara is able to do more with the controls. More jumps, climbs, etc. Fantastic, everywhere. She can now walk/balance on the poles you only used to swing on. Weapons are interesting. With the entire selection available from the start, unlike outfits you can use them all anywhere. They all (except her classic pistols) have limited ammo, and ammo cannot be found throughout the level. Levels are a good length as well. They are fairly restricted (corridor levels), but it's better than Legend. Longer than Legend, not as big as Anniversary. Overall, this one is my favourite. I couldn't decide between this or Legend, but this is great. The story is so intense and exciting, even though ocassionally predictable, I liked it. It tied together all loose ends, and didn't leave anything hanging. The level replay style is quite different to Legend and Anniversary becuase once you have played all levels, you revisit them exactly as you left them so there are no more enemies (except regenerative ones) and the puzzles are all already solved. This is the Treasure Hunt mode. If you want to replay a level with story as it was originally, you have to reload it from the load option within the game.  You have to play the other two first becuase the story won't make sense (although you may get away with not playing Anniversary...). There is less human fighting than Legend, but there is some. You mostly have to shoot spiders and bats. I would recommend this to any gamer, particularly if you like a good plot, action, combat, adventure, quiet solo play or Lara Croft. Only negatives would be restricted outfit selections and the rewards.

title: torchlight
text: Torchlight torchlight torchlight. I remember when this game first came out. Remember too? The graphics were just plain ugly even back then. Torchlight's history in short is that most of the Dev team worked on Diablo 1, 2 and every expansion in between. And that is exactly what makes Torchlight a complete failure. From the very first second I played it, I didn't like anything. The style, the visuals, the setting.... It feels rushed and unfinished. Normally I do a Pro v Con list but there are no Pros here, so here are just the worst things about Torchlight. - Linear Gameplay: I can't stress this enough, It may very well be the only thing that's absolutely wrong with this game but it's a big one. Ever played a 2D platformer, like Mario? Well that's just about as linear as you can get. Just go from start to finish, no deviation in between. To have something like that in a 3D game is... Why? But that's what Torchlight is, constantly. You go down and then you follow the path, follow it, kill every enemy you see and keep following the path. - Music: Well the town music is very similar if not the same as in Diablo 1 and 2. Because they hired the same guy to make the soundtrack. It shows, it isn't good. They probably thought that it'd be nice to have music that sounds the same as a far superior game. But by doing so, they hit the same note when an awful movie refers to a better movie during the movie. - Classes: Three character classes...? This is an RPG right? What kind of RPG only has 3 classes? Maybe Torchlight isn't the only one, but it should be. There really isn't an excuse for that, most RPGs already have the same classes over and over. But Torchlight takes the most generic 3 classes too, Melee Ranged and Wizard/Summoner None of which are any fun while running towards the next level down. - Graphics: I'm not a graphic freak, I honestly don't care about them, choppy framerate? I'm probably the last person to notice, but these GFX?! No! Just no, why is everything squareish? Was the Dev team all like "We need something round but a dodecahedron is easier to draw." I don't think so, don't like it Final verdict, Torchlight is nothing more than a Diablo clone. But I've played several clones in my day, this is by far the worst one. Torchlight feels like an empty vessel, like a game without a soul. It has no identity other than the one it tries to be. I heard that the sequel is far better.

title: torchlight
text: It's a nice Diablo clone, but a little too much Diablo and not enough Diablo and definitely not enough Torchlight. You get gems and sockets, transmutation, unique item drops or rares with random stats, town portal and identify scrolls, waypoints, hordes of mindless monsters, randomly generated dungeons, and skill trees. Unfortunately you lose out on multiplayer, varied environments, and a demon filled story to paste it together. Torchlight is not unique enough to not just be Diablo 2 version 1.x. And Diablo 2 version 1.x may still be better at being Diablo 2 version 1.x. That said, if you're a bit bored of killing the classic baddies of the Diablo series, but don't want to do anything unique either, this can actually be a bit of fun as a diversion. If you are a big fan of the genre there is never enough to go around. I hear Torchlight 2 is a big improvement. Diablo 3 has fairly well righted the ship. If you just want to loot all the things maybe even try Borderlands instead. 4/5

title: torchlight
text: *click*click*click* That's what you're going to be doing ALOT of in Torchlight. The game is an old school hack-and-slash RPG in the same vein as the Diablo series and all the clones that have spawned from that. Players who enjoy those kinds of games and/or are loot and stat junkies will absolutely adore Torchlight however everyone else will probably run out of steam once the main "story" is completed. There's tons of loot ranging from common stuff to rare items and sets of items to track down, you have three character types to choose from (the basic three: warrior, rogue, and wizard who each have three skill trees), you've got a pet that will carry loot and even transform into different things when you feed it fish, the different sections of the dungeon are artistically well done, and the range of enemies is definitely substantial. Other than being a solid dungeon crawler though there's not much else to attract those who aren't quite fans of that genre. The story is paper thin, theres absolutely no characterization in regards to your own avatar or the very few NPCs, the sidequests are uninspired (get this, kill that, go to a different dungeon and get this) and the whole thing just feels like a time sink - one that will definitely appeal to some but will leave others bored and ready to move on to something else after a couple of hours. The best way to really describe Torchlight: you're going to love it or hate it. Unfortunately I tend to put a good deal of emphasis on narrative, the game world, etc and this game just straight up doesn't have that.

title: torchlight ii
text: I don't like ARPG's. You just click till things die, and you click to to loot, you click, click and you click... I think, they are meaningless. Fun for a while, then boring and stale for the rest. All of them. But I absulately adore this game. Because, this game knows what it is; just guilty pleasure. Doesn't try to be serious and dark. Doesn't act like something that it is not.You can see it clearly in the art design, classes, gameplay, music and "story" parts.... I love this game because it is honest. I don't have too much play time on steam, but I played nonSteam versions of both I and II for a long time. I've played and just hated Diablo II and III. I've tried Van Helsing series and got bored to hell after a few hours. I've got hooked to Grim Dawn's intelligent class system, but got put off by endless undead and bleak art design after a while. But I always returned to this one with a smile. Don't get me wrong, I love dark and serious RPG's. But this is not a real RPG... Best part is; torchlight knows this too. All the charm comes form this very acknowledgement. If you like ARPG's, play this, this is a no- brainer... But if you are like me, and waiting for games like Tyranny and Tides of Numunera to come and save you from this long and RPG dry summer; give this one a shot. Torchlight II will entertain you untill a true RPG comes.

title: total war: attila
text: Okay now just to get this started, I did and sometimes still do play this game quite often, why, well lets talk about that. I don't play it for the great game that CA made, no, I play this for the mods it has, really good mods save this game for me. When I bought this I was thinking I'd try it maybe it's good, the only other thing I was considering buying was Shogun 2, which I had before (not on steam), but don't currently have. I was wrong, this game's grand campaign is quite boring for me, and to let you realize how, on strategy games like Stronghold and Battle for Middle Earth, I am the turtle player (you however won't beat me without proper siege). So for strategy games I play defensively and react to situations as they happen, doing this in Shogun 2 was really fun and necessary, here though it's boring. The ai will come at you quickly with half to full stacks, but beating them back is more a chore than anything else, only time you feel threatened is when they attack an unguarded settlement (which they will do a lot, if they can, but on base game, they basically just become annoying as they attack a settlement time and time again without taking it or destroying it). The combat ai is done fairly well, but that's well as in they know how best to charge you, they care little for skirmishing in sieges, they make a path into your settlement (wither that be with artillery, ladders, or rams), then charge in. When on the defensive unless they outnumber you on a minor settlement (in which case they may charge you), they sit around in defensive positions, so if you have missile superiority you can just pick them off without much worry. Now some of the grand campaign mechanics aren't that great, and the few that are good, may be a bit off. Example the fertility system, it's a nice system, makes end game harder, but some issues with it. One most of the regions become infertile by the end, and so I think that needs tweaking. Also every faction has sanitation buildings, such as canals and the like, now you'd think that an irrigated region would be more fertile right, nope. Unless you are I think it's Slavic, you have no way to increase the fertility of your regions, without mods that is. Also there is massive public order and squalor penalties for some things I can't quite understand, meaning you wont get the most out of your regions as you will probably build most regions the same way to keep everything running smoothly. So now lets talk about the stuff that makes this game actually worth playing for over 300+ hours, mods (you could say you are going for all badges and such, but that's game completion, doesn't mean you enjoy it). There is amazing mods for this game, you can find mods to overhaul most everything about this game. I play with mods that make the games more dynamic and diverse, also to make some things sensible. Like a mod that disables the loss of legacy tech as you progress the tech tree for romans, and making sanitation buildings provide fertility (sure the whole they lose sight of older tech as they change their ways is a nice thought, but don't take away the sanitation buildings, I prefer my aqueducts to having a bigger church, in fact I burned down all the churches in my playthroughs because the bonuses for Christianity suck compared to paganism, base game). So long and short of it, if you get this game, playing it a few times without mods wont be too boring, until you get to mid game. Playing it with mods may make it more enjoyable for you, however if you are deciding between this and Shogun 2, go with Shogun 2, it's much better in my opinion (the happiness system for shogun 2 is a bit too easy but the rest of the game is good). So I hope you find this somewhat enlightening, maybe I helped you decide on buying this or not, or at least prepared you for it. Also just so you know, I only have one of the culture packs (that being vikings), and no other dlc, cause I didn't want to spend anymore money on this.

text: This is a fantastic game. Truly. If you've played Rome/Rome 2, this really brings it full circle. Except, this time, you aren't watching shiny, well equipped and trained centurions and legionnaries bring all of Europe to heel. You're watching disorganized and undermanned men, who represent an empire that is quickly fading away. Seeing the Roman soldiers for the first time in this game is humbling. The sense of desperation as you cling to, not even relevance, but just pure survival, is immense. Or, perhaps, a game as the rising Sassanids or even as the Huns is more your speed. As I'm writing this, I am very tired, and so I do not have the time or energy to go into detail on why this game is great. But it is worth your time and money. Especially while it's on sale, so buy it fast! (Psst: Age of Charlemagne is 100% necessary)
